newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse tumbles, but ends off lows.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse tumbles, but ends off lows.

text.p: The Madrid bourse tumbled lower in thin volatile trade on Tuesday, but found the strength to pick itself up off session lows into the close. Dealers said there were no fundamental factors pushing stocks lower and the slump was purely a technical move.

The general index slid 10.23 points, 1.7 percent, to 589.81, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares fell 120.61 points, 1.77 percent, to 6,697.08 after touching 6,640.86 earlier. Next Ibex support is pegged at 6,620.

"This afternoon there has been pressure to sell from a chart point of view which together with doubts sparked by weakness in other stock markets has brought alot of paper onto the market, although we recovered a bit at the end," one dealer said.

Among individual stocks, Santander lost 3.86 percent to 4,105 pesetas despite announcing results at the top end of expectations. Santander said its net attributable profit had risen 30.2 percent to 59.78 billion pesetas. However, some analysts were concerned about a sharp rise in costs.
Other banks were equally depressed and BBV fell 120 pesetas to 3,970, while BCH slipped 170 pesetas to 5,800.

Zinc shares performed well for most of the session, boosted by a strong dollar and zinc price. However, Asturiana took a turn for the worse in late trade, to end 85 pesetas down at 3,265. Espanola del Zinc closed 15 pesetas higher at 2,025.
